How to get the cheapest long distance moving quote

Price the cheapest long distance moving quote for your home with the free calculator below: enter two ZIP codes and see your range in about a minute.

Estimator's noteShort moves are usually billed by the hour for the crew and truck. Long moves are priced by the weight of your things and the distance. Your ZIP codes decide which applies.

Your price shows before we ask for any contact details.

The cheapest long distance moving with a full-service crew costs $1,150–$2,350 for a studio and $2,600–$5,700 for a 2-bedroom home, priced for a 1,000-mile haul outside the busy season, with no stairs and no extra services. Movers charge by your shipment's weight and the miles it travels, so moving less, picking a quiet date and comparing written estimates bring the price down.

What a long-distance mover charges you for

To get the cheapest long distance moving price, know what the mover is charging for. Most of the bill is the line haul, the trucking charge, which the weight of your shipment and the road miles set; the weight chart below shows how it climbs. On top of that come loading and unloading, packing if you order it, and charges for stairs, a long carry from the door or a smaller shuttle truck where the big truck can't park.

The date matters as well. The calculator's rate table prices a July pickup higher at both ends than an off-peak one for the same 2-bedroom home, and full flights of stairs push the range up again, so the cheapest long distance moving date has no summer rush and the cheapest address has no stairs. Damage cover is part of the price too: released value comes free but pays no more than $0.60 per pound per article, and full-value protection costs extra.

Seven ways to cut a long-distance mover's price

Each of these lowers what a mover charges, and together they are how the cheapest long distance moving quotes are won:

  1. Weigh less. Sell or give away heavy things worth little, such as old furniture, books, gym equipment and garage tools. The cheapest long distance moving is a light one, since each pound left behind comes off a price set by weight.
  2. Pack it yourself. Packing service adds $500–$1,200 to a 2-bedroom move. Packing your own boxes removes that charge, though a claim for damage inside a box you packed can be harder to prove.
  3. Move off peak. A weekday in the middle of the month, from fall to spring, avoids summer's rush and the end-of-month peak.
  4. Take a wider delivery window. A mover that can carry your shipment on a truck with other households' loads may price it lower for a longer window. Get the window in writing.
  5. Clear the way for the truck. If a full-size truck can't reach your door, a shuttle truck and extra handling add a charge, so check parking and road access at both ends.
  6. Get three written estimates. Give each mover the same inventory, services and dates, so you can compare the cheapest long distance moving quotes like for like.
  7. Ask for a binding estimate. It fixes the price of the services it lists, so your cheapest long distance moving quote can't rise because the load weighed more than the mover guessed.

None of these steps costs anything but planning, and together they move the cheapest long distance moving price for your home toward the low end of its range.

When the cheapest long distance moving quote costs more

A quote far below the others can turn out to be the dearest by delivery day, so treat a cheapest long distance moving quote that looks too low with care. The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration lists the red flags: an estimate given sight unseen, by phone or online; no written estimate, or a price to be set after loading; a demand for cash or a large deposit; a request to sign blank documents; and a claim on moving day that you have more belongings than estimated. Read FMCSA's list of red flags.

On a move between states, the written estimate decides the cheapest long distance moving bill you can be held to. With a binding estimate, you pay its amount for the services listed. With a non-binding one, the mover can't make you pay more than 110 percent of the estimate at delivery, and any balance is billed afterwards. FMCSA explains binding and non-binding estimates. Before you sign, look up the mover's USDOT number with FMCSA.

Questions that expose a low quote's extras

Two quotes can only be compared when they cover the same things. Ask each company behind a cheapest long distance moving quote these questions, and get the answers in the written estimate:

  • Is the estimate binding, non-binding, or binding with a not-to-exceed cap?
  • Are stairs, a long carry, a shuttle truck and fuel already in the price?
  • What delivery window do you give, and what happens if you miss it?
  • Which valuation does the price include, and what does full-value protection add?
  • Will your own trucks and crews carry my goods, or are you a broker?
  • How much deposit do you take, and when is the rest due?

A company that won't put these answers in writing isn't offering the cheapest long distance moving deal, whatever its headline price.

Is a mover still the right call?

Even the cheapest long distance moving company costs more than a rental truck you drive yourself. A 3-bedroom home costs $4,000–$8,550 with movers over 1,000 road miles, off peak, before packing. What you get for that is a crew that lifts, loads and drives, and a mover that is liable for your goods under federal rules. If the estimates still run over your budget, the comparison below prices the same move with a truck and with a container.

Getting your cheapest long distance moving quote

  1. Enter your ZIP codes in the calculator above for a free range in about a minute. It needs no email.
  2. Cut the inventory before any mover sees it, since a survey prices what is there on the day.
  3. Book video or in-home surveys with three movers, and give each the same list and dates.
  4. Ask each one which estimate type it is giving, and what the delivery window is.
  5. Hold every written estimate against the calculator's range, and question any line that sits far outside it.

A written, binding estimate from a registered mover, close to the calculator's range, is the cheapest long distance moving price you can count on paying.

Key takeaways

The main numbers on this page, in a few lines.

  • Over 1,000 road miles, a typical 2-bedroom home of about 6,000 lb has a trucking charge of $2,200–$3,300 off peak, before loading, unloading and the first 50 miles.
  • With 3 movers, a 2-bedroom home move takes about 4–6.5 hours on site: $720–$1,800 off peak at 10 road miles.
  • Guides put a 2-bedroom home at about 40–90 boxes.
  • The moving checklist has 14 tasks, from 8 weeks before the move to after the move.
  • A move across a state line is an interstate move, so the federal rules for household goods movers apply.
  • A 2-bedroom home move takes up about 640–930 cu ft: the smallest truck that holds the heavy end is 20 ft.
  • Tip guides suggest $40–$100 per mover for each working day, to each crew: $40–$100 per mover for 4–6.5 hours on site, $120–$300 for 3 movers.
  • A 2-bedroom home move of 1,000 road miles, off peak: $1,340–$2,610 with a rental truck before help, and $2,600–$5,700 with full-service movers.
  • Long-distance movers price a move by your shipment's weight and the road miles, so every heavy thing you leave behind lowers the bill.
  • A flexible pickup date and a wider delivery window give a mover room to price your move lower.
  • Compare written estimates made after an in-home or video survey, never a price given over the phone.
  • A quote far below all the others is a warning sign, not a bargain.

From booking to final bill, in order

A low price only stays low if the paperwork is right. Use this list to book the cheapest long distance moving company you trust, check its registration, sign the bill of lading and settle the final bill.

0 of 14 done

8 weeks before

  • Paper or digital, keep every page a company gives you until the move is settled.

  • Look at how each one handled problems, not only at the star rating.

6 weeks before

  • On an interstate move, a binding estimate means you don't have to pay more than the estimated amount at delivery; added items or services, or something unforeseen such as stairs or a parking permit, call for a new binding estimate. Under a non-binding one, the mover can't require more than 110 percent of the estimate at delivery.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

  • Get the date, the arrival window and the price on paper or by email.

  • Know what it costs to change the date or cancel, and how much notice you must give.

  • Then compare it with the coverage the moving company offers.

  • Interstate movers must be registered with FMCSA: make sure yours has a U.S. DOT number. FMCSA's database of registered movers also shows insurance and complaint records.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

  • On an interstate move, the mover must give you a written estimate of all charges; a rate quote is not an estimate. FMCSA says to make sure it's based on an actual or virtual inspection of your things.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

2 weeks before

  • Aim to reach the new home before the truck does.

1 week before

  • Make sure someone can be at the new home on every day of the window.

The day before

  • So nothing holds up the end of the job.

Moving day

  • Ask about any charge you don't recognize.

  • On an interstate move, the mover must prepare an inventory of your things, and you both sign each page of it. You should get a partly completed copy of the bill of lading before the mover leaves your old home.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

After the move

  • After an interstate move, FMCSA says you have 9 months from the date of delivery to file it. List what's missing or damaged, and add photos.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

Rules that keep an interstate quote honest

Federal rules decide whether the cheapest long distance moving quote you sign is the price you pay. Here is what they say about written estimates, weighing, binding prices, delivery dates and the 110 percent limit.

  1. The mover must give you a written estimate

    The mover must do a physical survey of your household goods and give you a written estimate, based on it, of the charges for the move and all related services. You may waive the survey, but only in writing, signed before the goods are loaded.

    Source: 49 CFR 375.401 (eCFR, read 2026-10-28)

  2. You may watch the weighing

    You have the right to watch every weighing of your shipment. The mover must tell you where and when each one will happen.

    Source: 49 CFR 375.513 (eCFR, read 2026-10-28)

  3. A binding estimate covers the services it lists

    On a binding estimate, you pay the amount for the services it lists. Its face must say that it binds both you and the mover, and the mover may charge for writing one.

    Source: 49 CFR 375.403 (eCFR, read 2026-10-28)

  4. The bill of lading shows the pickup and delivery dates

    The bill of lading must show the agreed date or period for pickup and the agreed date or period for delivery, and then the actual date of pickup.

    Source: 49 CFR 375.505 (eCFR, read 2026-10-28)

  5. The 110 percent rule on a non-binding estimate

    On a collect-on-delivery shipment under a non-binding estimate, if you pay up to 110 percent of the estimate at delivery, plus charges for services you asked for after the bill of lading was issued and any charges for impracticable operations, the mover must hand over your shipment.

    Source: 49 CFR 375.407 (eCFR, read 2026-10-28)

More on these rules from the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration: Protect Your Move.

Tipping a long-haul crew

Tips sit outside any cheapest long distance moving estimate, and a long move may have one crew loading and another unloading. Work out what guides suggest for each mover, by the hour, by the day or as a share.

3 movers 4–6.5 hours

Per mover $40–$100

For the crew $120–$300

Who to tip and when

  • Tipping is up to you: guides call a tip a thank-you for good work, not an obligation. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides find cash simplest, handed to each mover at the end of the job. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House, MoveAdvisor and CNET)
  • When one crew loads and another unloads, guides suggest tipping each crew after it finishes its part. (HireAHelper, CNET, Real Simple, American Van Lines and NerdWallet)
  • On a move of several days, guides suggest tipping at the end of each day, in case the crew changes. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet and Forbes Home)
  • Guides suggest a separate tip for a separate packing crew. (CNET and This Old House)
  • Guides suggest asking the moving company about its tipping policy first: some build gratuity into the price, and some don't accept tips. (Forbes Home, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides suggest tipping more for stairs, heavy furniture or bad weather, and less, or nothing, for damage, a late start or careless work. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, CNET and Real Simple)
  • Drinks and snacks are welcome, but guides don't count them as the tip. (NerdWallet and CNET)

For it

  • Rental fleets are large, so a truck can often be booked at the last minute. (HireAHelper)
  • Rental companies have thousands of locations, so a truck is usually available nearby. (HireAHelper)
  • U-Haul's one-way rate is a flat rate that includes a set number of rental days and a mileage allowance for the route. (HireAHelper)

Against it

  • Even with hired help, the renter is still responsible for some heavy lifting and coordination. (HireAHelper)
  • Gas, tolls and mileage are paid on top of the rental. (U-Haul)
  • Rental trucks average only 10 to 12 miles per gallon of unleaded fuel. (moveBuddha)

For it

  • The company does all the hauling, even cross-country. (HireAHelper)

Against it

  • Movers offer valuation options that can reduce the out-of-pocket cost of replacing lost or damaged items. (FreightWaves)

Questions

How to get the cheapest long distance moving quote FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

Who is the cheapest long-distance mover?

No single company is cheapest on every route. Prices shift with your load's weight, the distance, the date and how full a mover's trucks are, so the cheapest long distance moving company for one household can be the dearest for the next. Compare written estimates for the same inventory and dates.

How do you compare the cheapest long distance moving quotes?

Give every mover the same inventory, dates and services, and ask for a written estimate after an in-home or video survey. Check whether each is binding, what valuation it includes and how long the delivery window is. A quote far below the rest is a reason to ask questions, not to sign.

Are full-service long-distance movers worth the price?

They cost most of any way to move: $5,700–$11,800 for a home of 4 or more bedrooms over 1,000 road miles, off peak. They are worth it when a self-move would mean weeks of packing, a large truck you'd rather not drive, or heavy pieces you can't lift. Packing yourself is the usual way to bring the bill down.

Is a long-distance moving calculator as good as a quote?

No. A calculator, like the one on this page, gives a range for homes like yours, based on size, distance and date. A mover's written estimate, made after it has seen your belongings, is the price you can hold it to. Use the range to spot a cheapest long distance moving quote that looks too good to be true.
